Privacy as a Fundamental Right:

• The Court held that privacy is intrinsic to liberty, dignity, and autonomy, protected under Part III (Fundamental Rights).

• It is derived from Article 21, but also linked to freedoms under Articles 14 (equality), 19 (free speech, movement, etc.), and the basic structure doctrine.

Overruling Earlier Precedents:

• The judgment overruled contradictory observations in M.P. Sharma (1954) and Kharak Singh (1962), which had denied privacy as a standalone right.

Impact:

This ruling laid the foundation for subsequent judgments like:

• Navtej Singh Johar (2018) (decriminalizing homosexuality).

• Aadhaar Act Case (2018) (balancing privacy with state interests).

Why Not the Others?

· Navtej Singh Johar (2018): Applied the privacy right to strike down Section 377 IPC, but did not establish privacy as a fundamental right.

· Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975): Dealt with electoral disputes and the basic structure doctrine, not privacy.

· Sunil Batra v. Delhi Administration (1978): Concerned prisoners' rights under Article 21, not privacy.

Turner syndrome occurs when a female has only one X chromosome instead of the typical two X chromosomes. This is represented in karyotype notation as 45,X (sometimes written as 45,X0), indicating a total of 45 chromosomes with just one sex chromosome (X).

The other options represent different conditions:

Disorder/SyndromeGenetic Basis
RetinoblastomaCaused due to deletion of a portion of chromosome 13.

Down's SyndromeA genetic condition that arises due to the presence of an extra chromosome 21. Chromosome 21 is repeated thrice (trisomy 21). Karyotype is represented as 47, XX, +21 (females) and 47, XY, +21 (males).
Klinefelter's syndromeAffects males. Genotype is 47, XXY, indicating the presence of an extra X chromosome. The extra chromosome arises from inability of X chromosome to detach during meiosis.

Can be inherited according to Mendel's Laws or arise from spontaneous mutation. Can involve a single mutation or multiple types of mutation in one gene.

Hypertension and diabetes are important risk factors.

Cause is multifactorial including genetic factors, environmental influences, and lifestyle. Type 1 is caused by destruction of beta cells of the pancreas. Type 2 is caused by impaired insulin secretion and peripheral insulin resistance.

Mathematically, it is expressed as:

Δx⋅Δp≥h/4π​

Cache memory is a small, high-speed memory located close to the CPU that stores frequently accessed data and instructions. Its primary purposes are:

· Speed Optimization: It provides the CPU with faster access to frequently used data than main memory (RAM), reducing latency.

· Performance Boost: By keeping commonly used instructions/data close to the CPU, it minimizes the time the processor waits for data (known as the "von Neumann bottleneck").

· Hierarchy: Cache operates between the ultra-fast CPU registers and slower main memory in the memory hierarchy.

Why other options are incorrect:

· The OS is stored in storage drives (HDD/SSD) and loaded into RAM, not cache

· Cache complements RAM but doesn't replace it (RAM is still needed for main memory)

· Cache is volatile and doesn't provide backup - it loses data when power is off

Additional technical details:

· Modern CPUs typically have 3 cache levels (L1, L2, L3)

· L1 is smallest/fastest (part of CPU core)

· L3 is largest/slowest (shared between cores)

· Cache uses SRAM (Static RAM) which is faster but more expensive than DRAM used in main memory

Cache memory is crucial for modern computing performance, helping bridge the speed gap between fast CPUs and relatively slower main memory.
